Schizochytrium sp. · Metabolic Engineering

Knockout target portfolio: modulating fatty acid composition

A standing hub for KO-engineering targets across #4, HS6, and #7 — sequence conservation, structure prediction, associated metabolic pathways, and directional engineering rationale for each target. Built out incrementally as targets are characterized; ELOVL6 (current #7 target) and PLD1 (already knocked out on #4) are the first two entries.

#4 · WT parent HS6 · EMS mutant #7 · KO strain
01

Framing: what "modulate fatty acid composition" actually means here

Every target on this page is being evaluated against a specific, stated engineering goal — not a generic "make lipids different." Two directional goals are both in scope, and they are not the same target list.

Two distinct, sometimes opposite directional goals

Goal 1 — increase SFA (saturated fatty acid) proportion: block the steps that convert saturated/short-chain acyl-CoA into longer or more unsaturated products.
Goal 2 — increase PUFA (DHA or EPA specifically): remove competition for shared precursors, or block degradation of the target species — critically, not knocking out the PUFA-synthase machinery itself, which would eliminate DHA/EPA production entirely.

EPA as its own trait axis, and phylogenetics as a standing dimension

This organism is best known for DHA, but EPA is a distinct, commercially relevant omega-3 with its own branch point in PUFA biosynthesis — worth tracking separately rather than assuming "more PUFA" is a single undifferentiated goal. Separately, placing each target's sequence in a broader phylogenetic context (not just 3-strain identity, but position relative to characterized orthologs from other organisms) helps distinguish real functional divergence from noise, and is applied here wherever a literature reference sequence is available (as with the PUFA synthase cluster below).

02

The actual DHA/EPA-producing machine: the PUFA synthase (pfa) cluster

KEGG's generic pathway maps (ko01040, ko00062) don't represent this pathway at all — Schizochytrium and other thraustochytrids don't synthesize DHA/EPA via the classical aerobic elongase-desaturase cycle. They use a distinct, three-subunit polyketide-synthase-like PUFA synthase (Metz et al. 2001, Science), first characterized in Schizochytrium sp. ATCC 20888 (GenBank AF378327–AF378329, proteins AAK72879.2/AAK72880.2/AAK72881.2). This is the pathway this project's earlier KEGG-map note flagged as "bypassing" the classical map — found here directly.

Confirmed by direct BLAST against the literature reference sequences, not domain inference alone

Domain-architecture searching (eggNOG Pfam hits: ketoacyl-synthase, acyltransferase, ketoreductase, dehydratase, phosphopantetheine/ACP-binding) surfaced several PKS-like candidates in this genome. Reciprocal BLAST against the actual ATCC 20888 reference proteins resolved which are real:

SubunitHS6 geneLocation#7 orthologIdentity to ATCC 20888 reference
pfaAg9189Scaffolds_24:1,345,047–1,354,067LOCUS_009783-RA83.1% / 81.5% (two segments, 99% coverage of the 2,911-aa reference)
pfaBg9191Scaffolds_24:1,367,104–1,373,208 (13 kb from pfaA)LOCUS_009784-RA75.6% (99% coverage)
pfaCg1343Scaffolds_11:240,403–245,811 (different scaffold)LOCUS_010992-RA80.6% (84% coverage)

Two other PKS-domain-containing genes surfaced by the initial domain search — a large gene pair on Scaffolds_9 (g15841/g15842, likely overlapping AUGUSTUS gene-model predictions at the same locus) and a small gene on Scaffolds_16 (g3540) — were tested the same way and ruled out: only weak, fragmented partial hits (25–35% identity) to the reference sequences, well below the clean near-full-length matches above. Annotated PKS-family domains alone were not sufficient to call these real pfa subunits; only direct comparison against the characterized reference did that.

Fully conserved between HS6 and #7

All three subunits are 99.2–99.8% identical between HS6 and #7 directly (not just similarly diverged from the reference) — essentially the same gene in both strains, including the same pfaA/pfaB clustering pattern independently observed in both genome assemblies. This is the actual DHA/EPA biosynthetic machine, and it is not a strain-specific difference; whatever separates these strains' lipid phenotypes, it isn't this pathway's presence or absence.

Reference sequences: AAK72879.2 (pfaA, 2,911 aa), AAK72880.2 (pfaB), AAK72881.2 (pfaC), Schizochytrium sp. ATCC 20888 (Metz et al. 2001). Confirmed by BLASTp, e-value <1e-20, against both HS6's and #7's independently predicted proteomes.

03

Putative knockout targets, separated by directional goal

The pfa cluster above is not a knockout target for increasing PUFA — disrupting it would eliminate DHA/EPA production. The targets below act on competing or flanking steps instead.

GoalGeneMechanismConfidence
Increase SFAELOVL6 / g12225Blocks C16→C18 saturated/monounsaturated elongation — C16:0 should accumulate at the expense of C18 products. Current #7 KO target (Section 5).Mechanistically direct; KO not yet built
Increase PUFA (DHA/EPA)ELOVL6 / g12225 (dual candidate)If ELOVL6 competes with the pfa cluster for shared malonyl-CoA/acyl-CoA precursors, knocking it out could redirect flux toward PUFA synthesis rather than away from it — the opposite framing of the same gene above. Genuinely open which effect dominates.Speculative, not mutually exclusive with the SFA framing
g4070 (ACOX1, KO K00232)Rate-limiting first step of peroxisomal β-oxidation. Knockout could reduce degradation of long-chain/unsaturated species, increasing PUFA retention — an established strategy in oleaginous-microbe engineering.Mechanistically plausible, not HS6-tested
PLD1 / g4538Already knocked out on #4 for stated composition-modulation goals (Section 6). Directional mechanism (toward SFA or PUFA) not yet established from literature or this project's data.Outcome-confirmed KO exists; direction unresolved
Ruled out: stearoyl-CoA 9-desaturase (KO K22770) is not a real HS6 ortholog

The original comparative-genomics KEGG map (report1.html §07) flagged an HS6-specific hit to K22770 without characterizing it further. Followed up here: pulled the actual reference protein behind that KO (M. tuberculosis Rv3230c) and BLASTed it directly against HS6's proteome. The two hits that came back (g71, g15628) are both only ~27% identity at ~57–59% coverage — well below a confident ortholog call — and both are independently annotated by eggNOG as flavohemoglobins (nitric-oxide dioxygenase family, KO K05916/K02613), not desaturase-system components. The weak BLAST similarity traces to a generic shared FAD/NAD-binding reductase domain, not real functional homology. This looks like the same low-confidence cross-reference artifact this project has hit before (ELOVL6's paralog confusion, the retracted missense survey) — reported here as tested and excluded, not left as an open lead. A genuine HS6 stearoyl-CoA desaturase, if one exists, has not yet been identified.

ko01040 — Biosynthesis of unsaturated fatty acids
Corrected render (the original comparative run hit a pathview rendering bug on this map and produced a blank image). 11 of the 32 KOs in this map are present in one or both genomes, concentrated in the very-long-chain fatty-acid elongation/β-oxidation machinery (ELOVL3/6, HACD, SCP2, ACOX1, ACAA1, ACOT7, HSD17B4) rather than the canonical Δ-desaturase steps — consistent with the PKS-based DHA synthase route bypassing this map's classical desaturase pathway, but not the empty map originally shown. 05

ELOVL6 — the current #7 knockout target

Full write-up: copy number, cross-strain structure, expression, the ELOVL family, and the KEGG annotation correction. (Migrated here from report1.html §11.5 — a short pointer remains there.)

11.5 — ELOVL6 knockout target: copy number, structure, expression

Requested follow-up on ELOVL6 (elongation of very long chain fatty acids protein 6), a live knockout target in strain #7. This directly follows up on Section 11.2’s blocked ESMFold attempt above — the same local ESMFold pipeline built for the HS6-vs-#4 project (public API down, local execution via HuggingFace transformers’ facebook/esmfold_v1) was reused here successfully.

Copy number in #7: one confirmed copy, with an annotation ambiguity worth flagging

#7’s own annotation (LOCUS_004835-RA, contig7:1,768,160–1,769,386) is a clean, high-confidence ELOVL6 call — correct PF01151 elongase domain, 100% self-identity as expected. A whole-proteome BLAST of this sequence against all 12,599 proteins in #7 turned up exactly one other hit above the family-domain background: LOCUS_010826-RA (“Baldspot”, 36.2% identity, 70% query coverage) on a different contig, which the automated pipeline also labels “Very long chain fatty acid elongase 6” despite the low identity and different gene symbol. Checking the neighbouring genes around the true ELOVL6 locus resolved this: LOCUS_004830-RA, five genes upstream, is a separate, distinct gene — “Putative fatty acid elongase 1” (SPAC1B2.03c) — not a second ELOVL6 copy. Conclusion: one true ELOVL6 copy in #7. The “Baldspot” hit is a different, more distantly related elongase-family member that inherited a generic functional description from automated annotation transfer, not a real paralog of this specific gene.

Sequence identity: fully conserved across all three strains, and confirmed against the actual knockout primer design

HS6’s ortholog (g12225, 408 aa) is 100% identical at the protein level to #7’s LOCUS_004835-RA (408/408 residues, no differences). The #4 (WT) reconstruction used throughout the HS6-vs-#4 project is in turn 100% identical to HS6’s sequence at this locus (consistent with that project’s finding that zero validated coding mutations exist genome-wide between HS6 and #4). ELOVL6 is therefore sequence-identical across #7, HS6, and #4 — a single conserved enzyme, not three strain-specific variants.

The user-supplied knockout primer design (ELOV6-F/Up-R/Down-F/R, targeting a 1,227 bp genomic sequence) was checked directly against #7’s LOCUS_004835-RA CDS: exact match, 1,227/1,227 bp, zero mismatches. The primers target the correct, verified gene, not one of the other elongase-family paralogs that share similar automated annotation labels.

Because the sequence doesn’t differ across strains, there is no WT4-vs-HS6-vs-#7 structural comparison to make here the way the missense-driven comparisons were attempted on the HS6-vs-#4 project — one fold applies to all three. It’s shown below for its own sake, as the first structural model of this gene in this project.

ELOVL6, ESMFold prediction (pLDDT 78, confident)
Confidence-colored (blue=high, orange=low). Compact, mostly-helical bundle consistent with ELOVL6’s known polytopic ER-membrane topology (GO:0005789). Two views, same model.
Expression: a modest, non-significant, time-fading trend — not a clean knockdown signature

In the HS6-vs-#4 (MT-vs-WT) time-course RNA-seq: overall genotype effect log2FC=−0.46 (down in HS6), p=0.032 but padj=0.18 — not significant after multiple-testing correction. Per-timepoint breakdown tells a more specific story: log2FC=−0.61 at 20h, −0.60 at 44h, fading to −0.15 at 68h — a real early/mid-timepoint trend that weakens by the late timepoint. The formal genotype×time interaction test is not significant (padj>0.99), so this pattern doesn’t clear statistical significance as a genuine time-dependent effect — reported descriptively, not as a confirmed finding.

ELOVL6 protein sequence, #7 annotation (LOCUS_004835-RA) and cross-BLAST results against both proteomes (#7 self-search, reciprocal HS6 search) available on request. ESMFold reproduction: same pipeline as documented in the HS6-vs-#4 project’s report4.html Methods section.

Catalytic mechanism: an illustrative view, not a docking result

ELOVL6 structure, rotating, with the conserved catalytic histidine-box highlighted
Magenta: the HWYHH motif at residues 256–260 — the histidine-box signature that literature on the ELO/ELOVL condensing-enzyme family (Denic & Weissman, Cell, 2007) identifies as the catalytic core for the first, rate-limiting step of fatty-acid elongation (condensation of malonyl-CoA with a long-chain acyl-CoA). Green: a schematic acyl-chain placeholder positioned near the motif to show where substrate engagement occurs — its exact position, pose, and conformation were not determined by docking or any energy-based method, and should not be read as a predicted binding geometry.
Why this is illustrative, not a docking pose

Unlike the g6124/g3557 kinase–substrate work in the HS6-vs-#4 project (a real protein-protein docking run, DFIRE-scored, hundreds of swarms sampled), this figure does not dock a substrate against ELOVL6. Small-molecule/lipid-substrate docking (e.g. AutoDock Vina against a malonyl-CoA or acyl-CoA ligand) is a different, untested pipeline in this environment and hasn’t been validated here. The histidine-box location itself is a genuine, literature-grounded structural feature; the substrate’s placement is a visual aid only, meant to show relative proximity to the catalytic residues — not a claim about binding mode.

Expression: #4 (WT) vs. HS6 (MT), all three time-course points

Note on scope: #7 — the strain where the ELOVL6 knockout is actually being made — has no RNA-seq data of its own. What follows is the HS6-vs-#4 project’s expression data, included here as the closest available reference because ELOVL6’s protein sequence is 100% conserved across all three strains (confirmed above). It describes this gene’s baseline expression behavior in a related strain pair, not #7’s own transcriptional state.

g12225 / ELOVL6, DESeq2-normalized counts
A consistent directional trend (lower in HS6 at all 3 timepoints, strongest early/mid, fading by 68h) that does not clear statistical significance after correction — reported as a real trend, not a confirmed difference.

Overall genotype effect: log2FC=−0.46 (down in HS6), padj=0.18 (not significant). Per-timepoint: 20h log2FC=−0.61, 44h=−0.60, 68h=−0.15. Formal genotype×time interaction test: padj>0.99 (not significant) — the fading pattern is descriptive, not a statistically confirmed interaction.

What a knockout would actually establish, given this data

Since ELOVL6’s protein sequence doesn’t differ between strains, a knockout tests something a natural mutation can’t: whether the enzyme is functionally necessary, not whether some existing difference already disrupted it. Two things from this project’s own data bear directly on interpreting a knockout phenotype: (1) three other elongase-family paralogs exist in this genome (below) — if any are functionally redundant with ELOVL6, the knockout phenotype could be partially masked; (2) this report’s own KEGG analysis (Section 7) already established that this organism’s DHA synthesis runs through a PKS-based route, not the classical ELOVL/desaturase elongation-desaturation cycle — so a knockout’s clearest effect is more likely to show up in membrane/storage lipid chain-length composition (C16→C18 conversion) than in DHA yield directly, absent evidence of pathway crosstalk.

The full ELOVL family in this genome: 4 paralogs, verified by direct BLAST rather than trusted from automated labels

Automated annotation across three independent sources (#7’s PGD pipeline, HS6’s eggNOG, HS6’s SwissProt/KEGG table) gave inconsistent names for the non-ELOVL6 genes in this family — e.g. the same gene called “fatty acid elongase 1” by one method and “elongase 3” by another, both pulling from different reference-organism naming conventions. Resolved here by direct pairwise BLAST against the confirmed ELOVL6 sequence and against #7’s whole proteome, rather than trusting any single label:

HS6 gene#7 orthologIdentity to true ELOVL6Verified identity
g12225LOCUS_004835-RA100%ELOVL6 (this gene)
g12221LOCUS_004830-RAn/a (distinct gene)ELOVL1/4-like — KEGG KO call ambiguous (K10247=ELOVL1 / K10249=ELOVL4, both assigned)
g1554LOCUS_010826-RA36.3%Distinct paralog (“Baldspot”-type) — eggNOG’s automated KO call of K10203/ELOVL6 for this gene is imprecise at this identity level
g7382LOCUS_005399-RA34.8%ELOVL4, confirmed directly (98.8% identical to #7’s own ELOVL4 ortholog) — the 1,234 aa length that first flagged this gene as an outlier is a real multi-domain fusion, not an annotation artifact
A correction to Section 7’s KEGG map: the confirmed ELOVL6 gene has no KO assignment at all

Section 7’s ko01040 map cites “ELOVL3/6” as present in this genome’s fatty-acid unsaturation machinery. Checked directly against this section’s findings: g12225 — the gene verified here as the actual, 100%-conserved ELOVL6 — has no KEGG_ko field in the eggNOG annotation at all. That map’s KO hit almost certainly traces to g12221’s ambiguous K10247/K10249 call or g1554’s K10203 call, not to the confirmed ELOVL6 gene itself. The biology (an elongase-family gene present in this pathway region) isn’t wrong, but the specific gene identity behind that KEGG box needs this correction — a good example of why this whole section verifies gene identity by direct sequence comparison rather than trusting a single annotation pipeline’s label, consistent with the rest of this report’s approach.

06

PLD1 (Phospholipase D zeta 1) — knockout already performed on #4

Unlike ELOVL6 (a planned #7 knockout), PLD1's KO was already carried out on strain #4, with the same stated goal: modulating fatty acid composition. Verified here against this project's genome/expression data.

Sequence confirmed: exact match, single locus

The #4 PLD1 protein sequence provided for this project (1,383 aa) matches g4538 in HS6's proteome at 100.000% identity across the full length, zero mismatches (BLASTp, e-value 0.0). eggNOG annotates it "Phospholipase D zeta 1," ortholog of Arabidopsis PLDζ1 (ath:AT3G16785). No second locus was found in the same identity range — single confirmed copy, same conservation pattern as ELOVL6.

Expression: #4 (WT) vs. HS6 (MT), all three time-course points

Same scope note as ELOVL6: this is HS6-vs-#4 project data, included as the closest available reference for this gene's baseline behavior, not #4's post-knockout expression (which this project's RNA-seq predates).

g4538 / PLD1, DESeq2-normalized counts
Flat, non-significant, no consistent direction across timepoints — expected, since this gene's expression was never naturally perturbed by HS6's mutagenesis; its KO on #4 was a deliberate, separate genetic intervention.

Overall genotype effect: log2FC=0.19 (up in HS6), padj=0.86 (not significant). Per-timepoint direction is inconsistent (up at 20h and 68h, flat at 44h) — no real trend, just noise around a stable baseline.

Structure prediction: not yet run

PLD1 is 1,383 aa — over 3× ELOVL6's length, and ESMFold's runtime scales worse than linearly with sequence length (ELOVL6 took ~21 minutes at 408 aa; PLD1 would likely take a couple of hours on this hardware). Held off pending a decision on whether the GPU time is warranted here; sequence identity and expression evidence stand on their own for now.
